project.name: llama.cpp
project.description: LLM inference in pure C/C++ with minimal dependencies. Supports multiple hardware backends (CPU, CUDA, HIP, Metal, Vulkan, SYCL, etc.), quantization (1-8 bit), and many model architectures.

RWKV v7 full recurrent architecture implementation using time-mix, channel-mix, and token-shift to maintain recurrent state across layers, inheriting from the RWKV v7 base class.
Shared base class for RWKV v7 family providing build_rwkv7_time_mix and build_rwkv7_channel_mix helper methods using recurrent memory context.
AR-WKV v7 variant of RWKV v7 architecture using RMSNorm instead of LayerNorm, with recurrent time-mix but standard FFN instead of channel-mix.
Cohere 2 model implementation with interleaved sliding window attention (ISWA) using RoPE positioning and standard GQA attention.
Step-3.5 model with ISWA, per-head Q/K RMSNorm, head-wise sigmoid gating on attention output, and variable-layer RoPE scaling.
OpenAI MoE architecture with ISWA attention, post-attention RMSNorm, and SwiGLU MoE expert routing using softmax weighting.
Gemma 2 variant with ISWA attention, input embedding scaling, attention-scale normalization, post-attention and post-FFN residual RMSNorm layers.
Gemma 3N multimodal model with ISWA, AltUp token prediction across multiple streams, Laurel gating, and per-head Q/K/RMSNorm with RoPE.
Gemma 4 with ISWA, per-layer rope frequency factors for proportional RoPE, per-head Q/K RMSNorm, and optional per-layer token embeddings.
MIMO2 model with ISWA supporting both dense FFN and MoE branches (sigmoid gating), with attention sinks for long context.
MiniCPM3 using LoRA-Q for query compression and MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention) for compressed key-value representations with separated RoPE and non-RoPE components.
SmolLM3 compact language model with standard self-attention, optional per-layer RoPE skipping, and SiLU FFN using RMSNorm throughout.
LFM-2 (Liquid Foundation Model 2) using hybrid memory combining recurrent and sliding-window attention, with template specialization for ISWA variant and optional dense or MoE FFN.
LLaDA diffusion-based language model using non-causal attention (no_cache), standard RMSNorm attention, and SiLU FFN, resembling LLaMA but with bidirectional diffusion.
LLaDA MoE variant combining the non-causal diffusion attention of LLaDA with per-token MoE expert routing and softmax gating.
MainCoder architecture with standard self-attention, per-head Q/K RMSNorm, RoPE positioning, and SiLU FFN using RMSNorm throughout.
Apertus architecture with per-head Q/K RMSNorm, per-layer RoPE factors, and custom xIELU activation (Extended IELU with per-layer alpha, beta, epsilon parameters) in the FFN.
Arcee language model with standard self-attention, RoPE, and ReLU squared activation in the FFN instead of the more common SiLU.
Bailing MoE model with standard self-attention, RoPE, and MoE expert routing using softmax gating and weights normalization in the FFN layer.
Bailing MoE v2 with grouped experts (chunked MoE), wqkv fused QKV projection, Q/K per-head RMSNorm, and shared-expert (shexp) FFN branches alongside MoE.
Deci model supporting hybrid attention modes: standard self-attention, linear (attention-free) layers, and no-KV (attention bypass) layers, with per-layer GQA and RoPE.
EuroBERT encoder model using non-causal attention (no_cache), RoPE positioning, and standard SiLU FFN with RMSNorm throughout.
Grove MoE architecture with per-head Q/K RMSNorm, RoPE, grouped experts (chunked by n_group_experts), and softmax-gated MoE FFN.
Hunyuan Dense model with per-head K RMSNorm normalization, per-layer RoPE factors, and standard SiLU FFN using RMSNorm.
Hunyuan MoE model with per-head K RMSNorm, per-layer RoPE factors, and MoE expert routing (SwiGLU variant) using softmax gating.
Kimi linear attention model using causal 1D convolutions for QKV projections (with persistent conv state), delta-net linear attention or MLA memory, and no RoPE; inherits from delta-net-base.
OpenELM model with fused wqkv projection, grouped query attention, per-head Q/K RMSNorm, RoPE, and optional per-layer attention skip connection.
Orion model using pre-norm (standard LayerNorm instead of RMSNorm), standard self-attention with RoPE, and SiLU FFN with residual connections.
AF-MoE (Adaptive Fusion MoE) with MuP scaling on embeddings, ISWA attention, per-head Q/K RMSNorm, attention gating, and dual FFN (dense + MoE) with sigmoid-routed experts.
PlaMo base model with standard self-attention, full-head RoPE (n_embd_head rotary dim), and pre-attention residual FFN (gating FFN output before attention).
PlaMo v2 hybrid architecture mixing Mamba recurrent layers and standard attention layers with SwiGLU FFN, inheriting from the Mamba base class.
PlaMo v3 with fused wqkv projection, per-head Q/K RMSNorm, template specialization for both standard and ISWA attention variants.
Position-based Language Model using LoRA-Q for query compression and MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention) for compressed key-value with separated RoPE/non-RoPE heads.
T5 encoder with relative position bias via build_pos_bias, non-causal attention (no_cache), and conditional FFN (ReLU for T5 or GELU-gated for Flan-T5).
T5 decoder with self-attention, cross-attention over encoder embeddings, relative position bias, and conditional FFN (ReLU or GELU-gated).
WavTokenizer decoder using transposed convolutions, positional net (PosNet) with GeGLU/gated conv blocks, and self-attention for audio token generation.
PaddleOCR multimodal model using multi-section RoPE (4 sections) for mixed-modality positioning, standard self-attention, and SiLU FFN.
PanGu embedding model requiring bias tensors on Q/K/V projections, standard self-attention with RoPE, and SiLU FFN with mandatory per-layer bias.
Delta-Net base class providing delta-net chunking for linear attention (chunk size 16 or 64), delta gating, and soft-max attention within chunks; shared by Kimi-linear and PLM.
SEED-OSS model with standard self-attention, optional attention scale, per-layer RoPE factors, optional Q/K/V biases, and SiLU FFN using RMSNorm.

data.summary: Auto-generated command-line argument parsing with help text generation. Parses CLI args into common_params struct. Supports flags, string/int options, value hints, environment variables, and preset-only options.
Declarations for CLI argument parsing. Defines common_arg struct (args, env, handlers, value hints), common_arg_utils helpers, common_params_context, and the parser init/sample/free API.

Core utility library: CPU detection, string helpers (format, split, strip, escape), filesystem utils (validate, create dirs, cache dir), timing (common_time_meas), model/context init helpers, batch utils, tokenize/detokenize, embedding utils, control vector loading, optimizer dataset init.

Central declarations for common utilities: common_params (300+ fields for all CLI options), common_params_sampling, common_params_model, cpu_params, timing helpers, string/fs/model/batch/vocab/embedding/control-vector/tMoE/training APIs, common_init_result wrapper.

Cross-platform console I/O with ANSI color codes. Supports simple and advanced readline modes with UTF-8 input, arrow-key navigation, history browsing, word jumping, tab completion callbacks, and spinner animations.
Console I/O declarations: init/cleanup, readline, display type (info/prompt/reasoning/user_input/error), spinner, completion callback, log/error helpers.
Async logging system with worker thread, ring buffer, log levels (DEBUG/INFO/WARN/ERROR/OUTPUT), color support, prefix/timestamps, and macros (LOG_DBG, LOG_INF, LOG_WRN, LOG_ERR).
Logging declarations: common_log struct, log levels, common_log_init/main/free/add/set_* API, LOG_* macros with verbosity thresholds, color constants.

Debug utilities: tensor data printing (common_debug_print_tensor) with type-aware float extraction, and ggml callback evaluator (common_debug_cb_eval) for inspecting tensors during graph execution with regex filtering.
Debug declarations: tensor printing template, ggml eval callback template, base_callback_data with regex tensor filters.

HTTP file downloader with progress bar, resume (ETag/Range), HuggingFace repo model selection (Q4_K_M, Q4_0, split GGUF), Docker registry GGUF resolution, and common_download_model that orchestrates HF/URL/Docker sources.
Download declarations: common_remote_params, common_download_model_opts/result, common_download_model, common_download_file_single, common_list_cached_models, common_docker_resolve_model.

HuggingFace cache management per local-cache.md spec. Resolves HF API commits, fetches repo file trees (LFS-aware), lists cached files, finalizes files (symlink or copy), and migrates legacy llama.cpp cache.
HF cache declarations: hf_file/hf_files structs, get_repo_files, get_cached_files, finalize_file, migrate_old_cache_to_hf_cache.
HTTP utilities: common_http_parse_url, common_http_client (httplib::Client wrapper with SSL/creds/redirects), common_http_show_masked_url. Inline header for URL parsing and client creation.

Sampling utilities wrapping llama_sampler: common_sampler struct with ring-buffer history, grammar support (LLguidance/LARK/re2), reasoning budget, all sampler types (top-k/p, temp, penalties, dry, xtc, infill, mirostat, adaptive-p). Implements grammar-first and resampling paths.

Sampling declarations: common_sampler wrapper around llama_sampler, init/free/accept/reset/clone/sample API, perf printing, candidate access, seed, sampler type name/char mappings, llama_sampler_init_llg.

Chat session handling with Jinja2 templating (chat templates, tools, thinking), PEG parser for output parsing (simple/native/gemma4), OpenAI compat (msgs/tools parsing), message diff computation, specialized template handlers (ministral-3, gpt-oss, gemma4), grammar-based generation.

Chat declarations: common_chat_msg/tool_call/tool/content_part/msg_diff, common_chat_params/format/tool_choice, common_chat_templates, templates init/apply/parse, reasoning_format enum, oaicompat helpers, template direct apply.

INI preset parser/writer for inference options. Loads presets from INI files, CLI args, cached models, and local models directories. Implements CSS-style cascading (base + added) and remote preset whitelist for security.
Preset declarations: common_preset (name, options map, to_args/to_ini/merge/apply), common_presets map, common_preset_context for loading/editing from INI/cache/models-dir/CLI with cascading.

UTF-8 parsing utilities for streaming: sequence length lookup, codepoint decoding with error handling (success/incomplete/invalid), completeness check, codepoint-to-UTF-8 encoding for all Unicode ranges.
Unicode declarations: utf8_parse_result struct, common_utf8_sequence_length, common_utf8_is_complete, common_parse_utf8_codepoint, common_unicode_cpts_to_utf8, common_unicode_cpt_to_utf8.

Declarations for auto-detection and parsing of chat assistant responses. Defines enums for reasoning modes (NONE/TAG_BASED/TOOLS_ONLY), content wrapping modes, call ID positions, and tool call formats. Core classes: analyze_base, analyze_reasoning, analyze_content, analyze_tools, autoparser, and peg_generator. Uses differential analysis to detect reasoning markers, content wrappers, and tool call formats from Jinja chat templates.

Helper utilities for chat auto-parser. Provides string trimming functions, diff splitting (LCS prefix/suffix computation with marker alignment), text segmentization (marker vs text), and template comparison utilities. The calculate_diff_split function finds the longest common prefix and suffix between two strings while aligning on marker boundaries. The segmentize_markers function splits text into MARKER and TEXT segments bounded by <> or [].

Code generator for auto-parser. The peg_generator class uses autoparser analysis results to generate complete common_chat_params with a built PEG parser arena. Takes a common_chat_template and generation_params, runs full differential analysis, and produces structured chat parsing rules for reasoning blocks, content wrapping, and tool calls (JSON-native, tag-with-JSON, and tag-with-tagged formats).

Implementation of chat auto-parser helpers. Implements string trimming utilities, diff split computation with marker alignment, prefix/suffix extraction functions, marker segmentization, whitespace pruning, and template variant comparison. The compare_variants function applies the same Jinja template with two different parameter sets and computes the diff between rendered outputs, enabling differential analysis.

Core differential analysis engine for auto-detecting chat template structure. Contains the full autoparser namespace implementation: analyze_reasoning (detects reasoning markers via template comparison with/without reasoning_content and enable_thinking), analyze_content (detects content wrapping), analyze_tools (detects tool call format - JSON-native, tag-with-JSON, or tag-with-tagged). Performs multi-phase comparison: reasoning presence, thinking enabled state, reasoning scope (normal vs tools-only), content wrapping, tool call format, function name markers, argument markers, call ID markers. Includes hardcoded workarounds for Qwen, DeepSeek, Granite, Cohere, Functionary, and other model templates.

Declarations for building chat-specific PEG parsers and AST-to-chat-message mappers. common_chat_peg_builder extends common_peg_parser_builder with tags for reasoning blocks, content, and tool calls (tool-open, tool-name, tool-args, tool-arg, tool-id, etc.). Provides standard builders for JSON tool calls (with nested/flat keys, function-as-key, call IDs, parameter ordering) and XML/tagged tool calls. Includes common_chat_peg_mapper (AST to common_chat_msg), tag_based_peg_mapper, and tagged_peg_parser for flexible tag extraction.

Implementation of chat PEG parser builders and AST mappers. Builds structured tool call parsers for JSON (function-is-key, nested-keys, flat-keys with parameter ordering), XML/tagged, and Python-style (LFM2) formats. common_chat_peg_mapper traverses the AST and constructs common_chat_msg with reasoning_content, content, and tool_calls. Handles monotonic JSON streaming by buffering arguments until tool name is known, normalizing Python single quotes to JSON, and closing unclosed braces. Includes Gemma4-specific mapper for non-standard JSON formats.

Declarations for the generic PEG parser framework. Defines 17 parser types: epsilon, start, end, literal, sequence, choice, repetition, and/positive-lookahead, not/negative-lookahead, any, space, chars (character class), string, until (delimiter), schema (JSON Schema metadata), rule, ref, atomic, and tag. Includes common_peg_ast_node/arena for AST construction, common_peg_parse_result with success/fail/need_more_input states, parse flags (lenient, debug), and builder with fluent API for composing parsers. Also defines JSON and Python value parsers.

Full implementation of the PEG parser framework. Uses a trie-based delimiter matcher for the 'until' parser. Implements UTF-8-aware any/char parsers. Supports partial/streaming parsing with NEED_MORE_INPUT result type. Atomic parsers suppress AST node emission on partial parse. Provides JSON (objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, null) and Python value parsers. Generates GBNF (Ginsburg Language) grammar output with lazy/trigger-rule support for constrained decoding. Supports JSON serialization/deserialization of parser state, and UTF-8 escape sequences in strings.

Declarations for converting JSON Schema to GBNF grammar for constrained decoding. json_schema_to_grammar converts a JSON Schema to a grammar string. common_schema_info probes schema structure (resolves refs, checks if resolves to string type). common_grammar_builder provides add_rule and add_schema callbacks. common_grammar_options supports dotall mode. gbnf_format_literal escapes literals for GBNF format.

Full implementation of JSON Schema to GBNF conversion. common_schema_converter handles all JSON Schema features: objects with properties/additionalProperties, arrays with items/prefixItems, strings with minLength/maxLength/pattern/format (date/time/date-time/uuid), integers with min/max constraints, enums, const, oneOf/anyOf/allOf, $ref resolution (including remote refs), and nullable types. Generates GBNF rules with builtin rules for boolean, number, integer, object, array, string, null, uuid. Also supports llguidance format output when compiled with LLAMA_USE_LLGUIDANCE.

Declarations for streaming JSON parser that heals partial JSON responses. common_healing_marker stores raw marker and json_dump_marker for locating healing position. common_json wraps nlohmann::ordered_json with optional healing marker. common_json_parse attempts to parse a potentially truncated JSON string, healing it by adding a marker and closing brackets/braces to produce valid JSON that can be parsed, while preserving the ability to cut again at the marker.

Implementation of streaming JSON parser with healing. Uses nlohmann::json SAX interface to find the error position, then heals by injecting a magic seed string as a marker. Handles partial JSON in object values, array values, object keys, strings, and unicode escape sequences. Supports high/low surrogate pair handling for partial unicode escapes. The healing marker allows both parsing the JSON and cutting it again at the same position.

Declarations for streaming regex matcher supporting partial matches. common_regex wraps std::regex with a reversed partial match pattern. Returns common_regex_match with type NONE/PARTIAL/FULL and capture group ranges. common_string_range represents [begin, end) positions. regex_to_reversed_partial_regex transforms a regex into one that matches on reversed input to detect partial final matches.

Implementation of streaming regex matching. Builds a reversed partial match regex: e.g., /abcd/ becomes ^(dcba|cba|ba|a) = ^((?:(?:(?:d)?c)?b)?a). Transforms character classes, quantified groups, alternations, parentheses, character escapes. Uses forward match on normal input and reversed match on reversed input to detect if a partial match reaches the end of pattern. Returns PARTIAL when the reversed pattern matches the reversed suffix but not the full forward pattern.

llguidance library integration for grammar-constrained sampling. llama_sampler_llg wraps the llguidance matcher (llg_new_matcher) as a llama_sampler. Converts the vocabulary to llguidance format by detokenizing all tokens. Uses llg_matcher_get_mask to compute allowed-token bitmask, setting disallowed logits to -infinity. Implements sampler interface: name, accept, apply, reset, clone, free. Tokenization uses llama_detokenize with special handling for zero-byte prefix tokens. Requires cmake -DLLAMA_LLGUIDANCE=ON.

Declarations for speculative decoding abstraction. common_speculative_type enum covers: NONE, DRAFT (separate draft model), EAGLE3, NGRAM_SIMPLE (self-speculative with history search), NGRAM_MAP_K (key-only ngram map), NGRAM_MAP_K4V (key+value ngram map), NGRAM_MOD (hashtable-based ngram), NGRAM_CACHE (cache-based). API: init, free, begin, draft (generate candidate tokens), accept (report accepted count), print_stats. Compatible with llama_context vocab checking.

Full implementation of speculative decoding with 7 implementation types. DRAFT uses a separate draft model context with vocab compatibility checking and token translation. EAGLE3 is a stub. NGRAM_SIMPLE searches token history for n-gram patterns. NGRAM_MAP_K uses common_ngram_map for key-only self-speculative decoding. NGRAM_MAP_K4V uses common_ngram_map with key+value statistics. NGRAM_MOD uses common_ngram_mod hashtable with Fibonacci hashing for open-addressing. NGRAM_CACHE uses common_ngram_cache with context/dynamic/static caches. Each implementation provides begin(), draft(), accept() virtual methods. Performance stats tracking (timing, token counts, acceptance rates).

Declarations for reasoning budget sampler that limits tokens in a reasoning block. State machine: IDLE -> COUNTING -> WAITING_UTF8 -> FORCING -> DONE. Tracks remaining token budget, watches for start/end token sequences, waits for UTF-8 completion before forcing, then forces a sequence of tokens. common_reasoning_budget_init creates the sampler. Supports explicit initial state for testing and cloning.

Implementation of reasoning budget sampler. token_matcher tracks sequential token matching for start/end sequences with reset on mismatch. State machine transitions: IDLE (watches for start_tokens), COUNTING (decrements budget, watches for natural end or budget exhaustion), WAITING_UTF8 (allows tokens to complete UTF-8 codepoint), FORCING (sets all logits except forced token to -inf), DONE (passthrough). When budget expires, optionally waits for UTF-8 completion before forcing end sequence. Provides name, accept, apply (logit masking), reset, clone, free sampler interface methods.

Declarations for n-gram cache-based speculative decoding. common_ngram holds 1-4 tokens. common_ngram_cache maps n-grams to empirical token distributions (token -> count). LLAMA_NGRAM_MIN=1, LLAMA_NGRAM_MAX=4, LLAMA_NGRAM_STATIC=2. API: common_ngram_cache_update (extract n-grams from token sequence), common_ngram_cache_draft (draft tokens from n-gram statistics), save/load to binary file, merge two caches.

Implementation of n-gram cache for speculative decoding. Updates cache with token sequences, tracking n-gram -> following-token distributions. Drafting uses dynamic (context) and static (corpus) caches with minimum sample size and percentage thresholds per n-gram size. try_draft validates drafts against static cache. Supports merging caches and binary file I/O. Implements self-speculative decoding where the model drafts tokens based on its own token history.

Declarations for two self-speculative decoding algorithms using n-gram maps. common_ngram_simple_config/configures ngram_simple mode. common_ngram_map is a map from n-grams to m-grams with key statistics (occurrence count, value distributions, acceptance counts). Supports optional hash map (COMMON_NGRAM_HASH_MAP_SIZE=262144) for O(1) lookup. COMMON_NGRAM_MAX_VALUES=4. API: common_ngram_map_begin (initialize from token history), common_ngram_map_draft (generate draft), common_ngram_map_accept (update statistics).

Implementation of n-gram map for self-speculative decoding. common_ngram_simple_draft: searches token history backwards for an n-gram matching the current pattern, drafts the following m tokens. common_ngram_map: uses LCG hash (prime=2654435761) for optional hash_map, maintains key (n-gram) statistics and value (m-gram) distributions with acceptance tracking. Supports context pruning on reasoning chat turns. Key-only mode drafts from most frequent following token; key+value mode considers multiple possible continuations with minimum hit thresholds. Tracks draft/acceptance statistics per value.

Declarations for common_ngram_mod, a simple open-addressing hashtable for n-gram storage. Uses Fibonacci hashing (multiply by 6364136223846793005ULL) for index computation. Stores n+1 tokens: n as key, 1 as value. Entry EMPTY=-1 indicates unused slot. API: idx(), add(), get(), reset(), get_n(), get_used(), size(), size_bytes().

Implementation of common_ngram_mod hashtable. Hash function: res = res*6364136223846793005ULL + token[i] mod size. Used by speculative decoding (NGRAM_MOD mode) to store n-gram -> next-token mappings with open-addressing and Fibonacci hashing.

nodes.summary: Jinja2 template parser. Consumes lexer tokens and builds an AST (jinja::program). Contains a recursive-descent parser class with methods for parsing expressions, statements (if, for, set, macro, filter), literals, binary/unary operations, and control flow. Throws parser_exception on syntax errors.
Parser declarations. Exports parse_from_tokens() function and parser_exception class. Depends on lexer.h, runtime.h, and utils.h.

Jinja template lexer. Implements the tokenize() method which converts a Jinja source string into a vector of tokens. Handles escape sequences, string/numeric/identifier literals, control sequences ({{, {%, {#), operators, brackets, and comments. No preprocessing is done to preserve source positions for error reporting.

Lexer declarations. Defines token struct with 30+ token types (literals, operators, keywords, brackets, control sequences). Exports lexer class with ordered_mapping_table for token matching and helper functions is_word/is_integer. Throws lexer_exception on errors.

Jinja runtime implementation. Contains execute_impl() for all AST node types: if/for/set/macro statements, expressions (binary, unary, member, call, filter, select, test, ternary), and literals. Implements built-in filters and tests. Uses context for variable scoping and gather_string_parts for output assembly.

Runtime declarations. Defines statement base class and 25+ derived types (expressions, statements). Key types: program, if_statement, for_statement, set_statement, macro_statement, member_expression, call_expression, binary_expression, filter_expression, test_expression, ternary_expression. Exports context (variable scoping) and runtime (execution) classes.

Jinja value type implementation. Defines ~15 built-in filters (abs, capitalize, replace, trim, join, batch, map, select, reject, etc.) and ~10 built-in tests (defined, none, boolean, string, number, sequence, mapping, iterable). Implements global_from_json for JSON-to-value translation, value comparison, and value_to_json for serialization.

Value type declarations. Base value_t polymorphic class with shared_ptr wrapper. Concrete types: value_int, value_float, value_string, value_bool, value_array, value_tuple, value_object, value_none, value_undefined, value_func, value_kwarg. Helper templates: is_val<T>, cast_val<T>, mk_val<T>. Also declares func_args, value_compare, and global_builtins.

String utilities implementation. Implements string_part and string class with is_input marking for security. Provides string transformations: uppercase, lowercase, capitalize, titlecase, strip. Handles hasher integration for hashing and mark_input_based_on for provenance tracking.

String declarations. Defines string_part (is_input flag + val) and string (vector of parts). Key feature: differentiates user input from template strings via is_input flag to prevent special token injection attacks. Exports uppercase, lowercase, capitalize, titlecase, strip transformations.

Capability detection implementation. Analyzes parsed Jinja programs to detect supported features (tools, tool_calls, system_role, parallel_tool_calls, typed_content, object_arguments). Uses stats tracking on value objects during template execution to determine which features are actually used by the template.

Capability declarations. Defines caps struct with boolean flags for ~10 supported features (supports_tools, supports_tool_calls, supports_system_role, supports_parallel_tool_calls, supports_preserve_reasoning, supports_string_content, supports_typed_content, supports_object_arguments). Exports caps_get() function.

Utility declarations. Provides string_replace_all(), peak_source() for error context display, fmt_error_with_source() for formatted error messages. Implements FNV-1a hasher struct (struct hasher) for value hashing with update/digest methods.

Jinja engine documentation. Describes architecture (lexer -> parser -> runtime -> value), input marking security feature for special token injection prevention, JSON-to-value translation, and how string provenance is tracked via is_input flag. References test-chat-template.cpp for usage examples.

data.summary: Main GGML header: core tensor types (ggml_tensor), 96 tensor operations (ggml_mul_mat, ggml_add, ggml_softmax, ggml_rope, ggml_flash_attn_ext, etc.), context management (ggml_context, ggml_cgraph), 42 data types including 20+ quantization formats (Q2_K through IQ4_XS), automatic differentiation, optimization API, ROPE types, threadpool, quantization API, SIMD intrinsics detection.

keyConceptsDetail.tensor: Multi-dimensional (up to 4D) data structure with shape, strides, data type, source tensors (graph edges), and backend buffer. Supports row-major layout with non-contiguous memory.
keyConceptsDetail.operation_graph: Function definitions create a DAG of tensor operations. Each tensor operation corresponds to a graph node. Graphs support forward and backward (gradient) computation.
keyConceptsDetail.quantization: 20+ quantization formats: Q1_0-Q8_1, Q2_K-Q8_K, IQ2_XXS-XS, IQ3_XXS-S, IQ4_NL-XS, IQ1_S-M, BF16, TQ1_0, TQ2_0, MXFP4, NVFP4. Includes importance-matrix aware quantization (IQ* types).
keyConceptsDetail.context_management: ggml_context manages memory pool and tensor graph lifecycle. ggml_cgraph holds compute graph with nodes and leaves. Work buffer for compute plan.
keyConceptsDetail.automatic_differentiation: Each tensor operation has forward and backward computation functions. Supports gradient accumulation, optimizer state (AdamW, SGD).
keyConceptsDetail.threading: ggml_threadpool with NUMA strategies, scheduling priorities, and polling levels for parallel computation.

data.summary: C++ wrapper providing std::unique_ptr smart pointer types for ggml C objects: ggml_context, gguf_context, ggml_gallocr, ggml_backend, ggml_backend_buffer, ggml_backend_event, ggml_backend_sched.

Graph allocator for GGML: one-shot memory allocator with no scratch buffer. Provides ggml_tallocr (tensor allocator) and ggml_gallocr (graph allocator). Supports pre-allocation via worst-case graphs, automatic reallocation on topology change, and multi-buffer allocation with per-node buffer assignment.

Backend abstraction layer: CPU, CUDA, Metal, Vulkan, SYCL, OpenCL, etc. Provides buffer types, device enumeration, backend scheduler for multi-device tensor parallelism, event-based synchronization, async tensor copy, graph plan caching, and dynamic backend loading from shared libraries.
BLAS backend: provides ggml_backend_blas_init() for OpenBLAS/BLIS-backed matrix multiplication acceleration. Thread count for FP32 conversion and BLAS ops is configurable.
Huawei CANN backend (Ascend NPU): supports up to 16 CANN devices. Provides device management, HBM memory info, pinned host buffer, and per-device buffer types. Implements ggml_backend interface.

CPU backend: SIMD intrinsics detection (SSE3/AVX/AVX2/AVX512/NEON/SVE/SME/RISCV_V/VSX/WASM), threadpool management, NUMA support, graph compute plan with work buffer, i32/f32 tensor get/set, FP16/BF16 conversion, reference implementations via ggml_type_traits_cpu.

NVIDIA CUDA backend: GPU inference on CUDA/ROCm/MUSA. Supports up to 16 devices, multi-GPU tensor parallelism via split buffer, pinned host memory, cuBLAS/hipBLAS/muBLAS integration, allreduce for tensor parallelism, host buffer registration.
Qualcomm Hexagon DSP backend: enables GGML graph computation on Hexagon DSP hardware via the Qualcomm AI Engine.
Apple Metal backend: GPU inference on macOS/iOS via Metal. Supports Metal family checking, command buffer capture, abort callback, dynamic library loading.
OpenCL backend: GPU inference via OpenCL framework. Provides device buffer type and pinned host buffer type.
Intel OpenVINO backend: CPU inference via Intel OpenVINO toolkit. Supports multi-device configuration, host buffer type per device, buffer type per device.

High-level training API: datasets, forward/backward/optimizer graphs, AdamW and SGD optimizers, loss functions (cross-entropy, MSE), gradient accumulation, result tracking (accuracy). Integrates with backend scheduler. Provides high-level ggml_opt_fit() and ggml_opt_epoch() functions.
RPC backend for distributed inference: connects to remote servers via endpoint (proto v3.6.1), supports up to 16 servers. Allows offloading computation to remote devices.
Intel SYCL backend: GPU inference via Intel SYCL (oneAPI). Supports up to 48 SYCL devices, multi-device tensor parallelism via split buffer, pinned host memory, device enumeration and memory info.
Virtual GPU backend: minimal header providing backend registration entry point for a virtualized GPU implementation.
Vulkan backend: GPU inference via Vulkan API. Supports up to 16 Vulkan devices, device memory info, host pinned buffer, dynamic library loading.
WebGPU backend: browser-based GPU inference via WebGPU API. Allows GGML graphs to run in web browsers.
IBM zDNN backend: neural network acceleration on IBM Z hardware via zDNN library.
AMD ZenDNN backend: neural network acceleration on AMD Zen processors via ZenDNN library. Configurable thread count for ZenDNN operations.

GGUF model file format: binary serialization for GGML models. Structure: magic, version, tensor count, KV pairs, tensor metadata (name, shape, type, offset), optional aligned data blob. Supports typed KV data (uint/int/float/bool/string/array), tensor type/offset queries, file I/O (single-pass write, split meta/data write), context initialization with optional embedded ggml_context.

Core GGML implementation: tensor operations (all 96 ops including ggml_mul_mat, attention variants, state space models, RWKV, gated attention), context/tensor lifecycle, compute graph building, backward pass, SIMD kernels (AVX/AVX2/AVX512/NEON/SVE/SME), memory management, type size calculations, threadpool implementation.
GGML C++ utilities: terminate handler for uncaught C++ exceptions during compute, backtrace printing. Heavily uses ggml-impl.h.

Graph allocator implementation: one-shot allocator with no scratch buffer. Supports in-place operation detection, aligned offset computation, tensor allocation via backend buffer, dynamic buffer chunks for graph re-allocation, and reserve/pre-allocate for worst-case graphs. Handles multi-buffer allocation with per-node and per-leaf buffer assignment.

Quantization kernels: reference implementations and optimized SIMD kernels for all quantization formats. Supports Q1_0-Q8_1, Q2_K-Q8_K, IQ2_XXS-XS, IQ3_XXS-S, IQ2_XXS-S, IQ4_NL-XS, IQ1_S-M, TQ1_0, TQ2_0, MXFP4, NVFP4, BF16. Includes quantization (float to quantized), dequantization (quantized to float), importance-matrix aware quantization, IQ initialization (lookup tables for 2/3-bit).

Quantization function declarations: row-wise quantization (Q1_0/Q4_0/Q4_1/Q5_0/Q5_1/Q8_0/Q8_1, K variants, IQ* types, TQ, MXFP4, NVFP4), dequantization, and importance-matrix aware quantization. Includes IQ lookup table initialization.

GGML backend registry and management. Defines backend registration API (ggml_backend_t, ggml_backend_reg_t), scheduler for multi-backend graph execution, and the default CPU backend. Core functions: ggml_backend_init_all(), ggml_backend_init(), ggml_backend_free(), ggml_backend_get_type(), ggml_backend_reg_get_n(), ggml_backend_reg_get_name(), ggml_backend_reg_get_backend_i().

Backend registration and dynamic loading. Manages ggml_registered_backends[], loads backends from shared libraries via dlopen/dlsym, calls backend init/fini entry points. Supports registering backends at runtime with GGML_REGISTER_BACKEND macro.

Meta backend for multi-device support. Implements a forwarding backend that delegates to other backends (CPU or GPU) based on device affinity. Supports memory mapping, device buffers, and device-specific graph partitioning via ggml_backend_meta_t interface.

Dynamic loading wrapper for backend shared libraries. Wraps dlopen/dlsym calls and provides ggml_backend_dl_init() function. Dynamically loads backend shared objects and resolves the backend entry point.
Declarations for the dynamic loader backend. Defines ggml_backend_dl_init() and related structures used by ggml-backend-dl.cpp for runtime backend loading.

Backend implementation interface definitions. Declares ggml_backend_t and ggml_backend_i interface structures with function pointers for graph computation, memory allocation, tensor operations, and synchronization. The main interface struct is ggml_backend_i with callbacks: graph_compute, get_alignment, alloc_buf,free_buf, get_no_alloc, set_no_alloc, get_tensor, cpy_tensor_async, sync, event record/wait.

GGML graph optimization passes. Implements graph transformations: vertical fusion (merging adjacent ops), horizontal fusion (combining ops with same inputs), and node elimination (removing no-op and redundant copy nodes). Key functions: ggml_graph_compute_forward_opt(), opt_params struct with flags to control optimization levels (FUSION, COPIES).

GGUF (GGML Universal File) format reader and writer. Handles serialization/deserialization of model metadata, tensors, and KV caches. Defines gguf_init/meta/free functions, gguf_get/put_tensor methods for reading/writing tensor data, and KV cache operations. Supports reading GGUF files into ggml_context via gguf_load_model().

Common GGML definitions shared across backends. Defines quantization types (GGML_TYPE_Q4_0, Q4_1, Q5_0, Q5_1, Q8_0, Q8_1, Q2_K, Q3_K, Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K, IQ4_NL, IQ4_XS, IQ1_S, IQ2_XXS, IQ2_XS, IQ3_XXS, IQ3_S, IQ1_S, F16, BF16, F32, F64, I8, I16, I32, I64), type traits, arithmetic and comparison ops, SIMD kernel dispatch, and common utility macros used throughout GGML.
Threading declarations. Declares thread pool initialization, dispatch, and cleanup functions used for parallel execution of graph nodes across multiple CPU threads.
Thread pool implementation. Provides ggml_threadpool_t abstraction for parallel task execution. Creates and manages worker threads, dispatches tasks in parallel, and handles thread pool shutdown.

GGML extension API for custom backends. Declares ggml_ext_t interface allowing third-party backends to register custom graph optimizations and transformations via ggml_register_ext(). Provides a plugin mechanism for extending GGML functionality.

GGML implementation details and internal structures. Defines ggml_context, ggml_tensor, ggml_cgraph, ggml_scratch, ggml_backend_buffer, and other core runtime structures. Also defines ggml_compute_params, compute functions (ggml_compute_forward_*), and ggml_init_params. This is the central internal header defining all runtime data structures used by the GGML compute graph engine.
Main CPU backend implementation with BLAS support, thread pool management, atomic operations, and compute dispatch for all GGML tensor operations.
CPU backend registration and dispatch - implements ggml-backend interface, registers extra buffer types (AMX, KleidiAI, Spacemit, repack), manages device initialization.
Dispatcher for quantized matmul kernels - routes to architecture-specific implementations based on compile flags (x86, ARM, PPC, etc.).
Declarations for all quantization functions (quantize_row_*, ggml_vec_dot_*) for standard and K-quants, plus generic fallbacks.
SIMD operations dispatch table - implements forward compute functions for all GGML operations (norm, rope, attention, etc.) with architecture-specific SIMD optimizations.
Declarations for all ggml_compute_forward_* functions implementing tensor operations.
SIMD vector operations implementation for fp32/fp16/bf16 dot products using SVE, RVV, and other SIMD intrinsics.
SIMD vector header with all inline implementations for AVX, AVX2, AVX512, NEON, SVE, SVE2, WASM SIMD, RVV, and scalar fallbacks.
Common CPU utilities including type conversion helpers, thread range calculation, and flash attention tile configuration.
CPU implementation interface - defines ggml_compute_params, SIMD type aliases (m512bh, m512i), 32-bit ARM NEON compatibility shims.
Binary SIMD operations (add, sub, mul, div) with Accelerate framework support on macOS.
Declarations for binary tensor operations (add, sub, mul, div).
Unary SIMD operations (abs, neg, tanh, sigmoid, exp, sqrt, etc.) with architecture-specific vectorization.
Declarations for unary tensor operations (abs, sigmoid, tanh, exp, sqrt, etc.).
Weight repacking for quantization - interleaves blocks for optimized matmul access patterns. Includes generic and RISC-V (__riscv_zvfh) implementations.
Repack declarations and block data structures for quantized weight interleaving (block_q4_Kx8, block_q8_Kx4, etc.).
Type traits implementation for CPU extra buffer types - routes compute to specialized backends (AMX, KleidiAI, Spacemit).
Type traits declarations - defines tensor_traits and extra_buffer_type abstract interfaces.
SIMD GEMM (matrix multiply) kernels for fp32 with configurable tile sizes based on architecture (AVX512, AVX2, NEON, scalar).
SIMD architecture detection and mapping macros - defines GGML_F32_VEC, GGML_F16_VEC, etc. for SVE, NEON, RVV, AVX, AVX2, AVX512, WASM, Power9, RISC-V ZFHmin.
x86 SIMD quantized matmul kernels using AVX, AVX2, AVX512 for all quantization types (Q1-Q8, K-quants, IQ variants).
x86/x86_64 CPU feature detection via CPUID - detects SSE, AVX, AVX2, AVX512, AMX, VNNI, F16C, BMI2 and AMD-specific features.
x86 weight repacking with AVX/AVX2/AVX512 F16C optimizations for FP16 conversion and interleaved block layout.
ARM NEON quantized matmul kernels for Q4-Q8, K-quants, and IQ variants using ARM NEON SIMD intrinsics.
ARM aarch64 CPU feature detection - detects dotprod, FP16 vector arith, SVE, SVE2, I8MM, SME via hwcap/sysctl.
ARM weight repacking with NEON, MATMUL_INT8, DOTPROD for optimized block interleaving.
PowerPC quantized matmul using POWER9+ VSX (Vector Scalar Extension) SIMD intrinsics.
PowerPC CPU detection - identifies POWER version (7-11) and VSX availability via AT_PLATFORM auxv.
IBM s390x quantized matmul using VXE/VXE2 (Vector Extension) SIMD for z15+ and NNPA for z16+.
s390x CPU feature detection - identifies VXE2 and NNPA support via hwcap (HWCAP_VXRS_EXT2, HWCAP_NNPA).
RISC-V quantized matmul using RVV (RISC-V Vector Extension) intrinsics with variable vector length.
RISC-V 64-bit CPU detection via riscv_hwprobe syscall - identifies RVV (RISC-V Vector) availability.
RISC-V weight repacking using RVV intrinsics for 4x8 block interleaving of Q8_0 quantized weights.
LoongArch quantized matmul using LSX (LoongArch SIMD) intrinsics (__lsx_vmulwev_h_b, etc.).
WebAssembly quantized matmul using wasm SIMD128 intrinsics (wasm_f32x4_*, wasm_i32x4_*).
Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) backend for Sapphire Rapids - implements tile-based int8 matmul with __AMX_INT8__.
AMX backend declarations - conditional compilation for __AMX_INT8__ and __AVX512VNNI__.
KleidiAI micro-kernels for ARM - optimized matmul using SME2, SVE, NEON DOTPROD, I8MM for Q4/Q8 quantized inference.
KleidiAI integration layer for ARM - CPU feature detection (SME, SVE, I8MM, DOTPROD) and kernel dispatch.
Llamafile optimized SGEMM (fp32 matrix multiply) - multithreaded contiguous GEMM with AVX512/NEON/VXE/RVV support.
Spacemit IME (Integer Matrix Engine) for RISC-V - quantized GEMM using Spacemit X1850's proprietary extension.

nodes.summary: Main NVIDIA CUDA backend implementing GGML tensor operations via cuBLAS and custom CUDA kernels for all operation types.
CUDA matrix multiplication kernels including FP16, BF16, FP8, and quantized GEMM implementations with tiling andwarps.
CUDA mixed-precision matmul kernels for Q4_K, Q5_K, and Q6_K quantization formats on NVIDIA GPUs.
CUDA Flash Attention kernels implementing Fused Attention (Flash Attention v2) for transformer models on NVIDIA GPUs.
Data type conversion kernels for CUDA: converts between FP16, BF16, FP32, and quantized formats on the GPU.
Memory copy kernels for CUDA tensor transfers between host and device memory with async support.
CUDA softmax and cross-entropy loss kernels for efficient normalization on NVIDIA GPUs.
CUDA normalization kernels (RMSNorm, LayerNorm) and state-space model operations on NVIDIA GPUs.
CUDA Rotary Positional Embedding (RoPE) kernels supporting standard, YaRN, and long-ring implementations.
CUDA embedding lookup kernels (getrows) for efficient token embedding retrieval on NVIDIA GPUs.
CUDA im2col kernels for converting image patches to columns for convolution operations on NVIDIA GPUs.
CUDA 2D convolution kernels including depthwise, transpose, and dilated variants for NVIDIA GPUs.
GPU quantization kernels for converting FP32/FP16 weights to Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K and other formats on NVIDIA GPUs.
CUDA vendor header providing native NVIDIA CUDA API bindings: cuBLAS, cuDNN, and runtime APIs.
HIP vendor header providing AMD HIP/ROCm API bindings as a drop-in CUDA replacement via macro remapping.
MUSA vendor header providing Moore Threads MUSA API bindings as a CUDA-compatible abstraction layer.
Apple Metal shader library with GPU kernels for all GGML operations: matmul, attention, softmax, norm, RoPE, quantization.
Apple Metal backend implementation: buffer management, tensor transfer, device enumeration, and kernel dispatch.
Metal device management: GPU device enumeration, memory allocation, shared buffers, and device property queries.
Metal operation dispatch: bridges GGML tensor operations to Metal compute shader kernels.
Metal backend common utilities: helper functions, tensor accessors, and shared kernel compilation routines.
Vulkan compute shader backend implementing all GGML operations via SPIR-V shaders on GPUs supporting Vulkan.
Intel SYCL backend implementing GGML operations via oneAPI/DPC++ for Intel CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators.
Huawei CANN backend using Ascend NPU ACLNN APIs to implement GGML tensor operations on Ascend hardware.
ACLNN operation wrappers bridging GGML tensor operations to Huawei Ascend NPU ACLNN library calls.
Tensor abstraction layer for CANN: manages Ascend tensor descriptors and data layout conversions.
Intel OpenVINO backend implementing GGML operations via OpenVINO inference runtime for CPU/GPU/VPU.
BLAS backend implementing GGML matrix operations via cuBLAS, OpenBLAS, or other BLAS libraries.
RPC backend enabling distributed GGML inference by forwarding tensor operations over network sockets.
Qualcomm Hexagon DSP backend implementing GGML operations via the Hexagon Tensor Processor (HTP) interface.
Hexagon HTP driver: manages DSP runtime, memory allocation, and kernel dispatch for Qualcomm Hexagon.
WebGPU backend implementing GGML operations via WebGPU compute shaders in browsers and WASM environments.
AMD ZenDNN backend using AMD Zen Deep Neural Network library for optimized GGML operations on AMD EPYC CPUs.
IBM zDNN backend using IBM zAIU (z Deep Neural Network) library for GGML operations on IBM Z mainframe hardware.
OpenCL backend implementing GGML tensor operations via OpenCL compute kernels for broad GPU compatibility.
Virtual GPU backend using VirGL for hardware-accelerated rendering and GGML inference in virtualized environments.
VirtGPU APIR backend dispatcher: dynamically loads a GGML backend library and remotes API calls over VirGL.

data.summary: Converts HuggingFace model format to GGUF format for use with llama.cpp. Defines ModelBase and model-specific subclasses (TextModel, MmprojModel) with tensor mapping, vocabulary handling, and metadata writing.
Converts LoRA adapter weights to GGUF format. Defines LoraTorchTensor for tensor manipulation and handles LoRA A/B weight decomposition.
Converts old ggml format files (GGML, GGMF, GGJT variants) to GGUF format. Handles legacy tensor types and vocab formats.
Updates convert_hf_to_gguf.py with new tokenizer pre-tokenizer hashes. Downloads tokenizers from HuggingFace and generates get_vocab_base_pre() function for new models.
GGUF Python package entry point. Re-exports all public APIs from submodules: constants, lazy, gguf_reader, gguf_writer, quants, tensor_mapping, vocab, utility, metadata.
Compatibility shim. Redirects imports to the gguf package root (gguf/__init__.py). Left for backward compatibility with code importing gguf/gguf.py directly.
GGUF file reader supporting reading and modification of GGUF files. Defines ReaderField and ReaderTensor structures, handles field/tensor iteration, alignment, and endianness.
GGUF file writer for creating GGUF files. Handles KV data, tensor info, weight writing, shard splitting, endianness, and file state management.
Vocabulary handling for GGUF tokenizers. Supports SPM (SentencePiece), BPE, and special vocab loading. Integrates with mistral-common for Tekken and Mistral tokenizers.
GGUF constants: magic number, version, alignment, quantization sizes, metadata keys (Keys.General, Keys.Architecture), tensor types, rope scaling, pooling types, and model architectures.
Quantization utilities for GGUF tensor encoding/decoding. Defines quantization classes (Q4_0, Q4_1, Q5_0, Q5_1, Q8_0, Q2_K, Q3_K, Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K, etc.) with serialize/deserialize methods.
Model metadata handling: loads authorship info from model cards, HuggingFace parameters, generation configs, and metadata override files. Maps to GGUF KV store format.

Maps tensor names between different model formats and GGUF conventions. Defines TensorNameMap for embedding, attention, FFN, rope, and output tensors across llama, gptneox, gpt-j, bloom, falcon, qwen, phi, mamba, and other architectures.
Lazy tensor loading infrastructure. Defines LazyBase, LazyNumpyTensor, LazyTorchTensor with metaclass-based operator overloading for deferred computation on tensor metadata.
Utility functions: filename templating, model size labeling, naming conventions, and remote safetensor file handling for HuggingFace models.

Python package configuration for gguf library v0.18.0. Defines dependencies: numpy, tqdm, pyyaml, requests, sentencepiece (optional), PySide6 (optional GUI). Defines CLI entry points for gguf-convert-endian, gguf-dump, gguf-set-metadata, gguf-new-metadata, gguf-editor-gui.

nodes.summary: Root CMake build configuration. Sets up CMAKE module path, defines build options (LLAMA_BUILD_TESTS, LLAMA_BUILD_SERVER, GGML_CUDA, GGML_VULKAN, etc.), includes cmake/build-info.cmake and cmake/common.cmake, adds ggml/, src/, common/, tests/, examples/ subdirectories, and configures install targets.
CMake presets for x64-linux-gcc (debug/release/static), x64/arm64-windows-llvm, arm64-apple-clang, x64-windows-msvc, x64-windows-sycl, x64-windows-vulkan with preset inheritance chains.

Python package config for model conversion scripts (llama-cpp-scripts). Depends on numpy, sentencepiece, transformers, protobuf, torch (from pytorch CPU-only source), and local gguf-py package. Provides CLI entry points for convert_hf_to_gguf, convert_lora_to_gguf, convert_llama_ggml_to_gguf, ggml_vk_generate_shaders.
Python linting config (flake8). Max line length 125, ignores E203/E501/etc. Excludes examples/, tools/, __init__.py, .git, __pycache__, build/, dist/.

C++ code formatting rules. 4 spaces, brackets on same line, column limit 120, C++17 standard, breaks before braces, align trailing comments, insert braces, LF line endings, includes CUDA attribute macros (__host__, __device__, __global__, __forceinline__, __launch_bounds__).

C++ static analysis config. Enables bugprone-*, readability-*, clang-analyzer-*, performance-*, portability-*, misc-* checks with exclusions for easily-swappable-parameters, narrowing-conversions, identifier-length, implicit-bool-conversion, etc. FormatStyle: none.

Server CI/CD workflow. Triggers on push to master and PRs touching server code. Jobs: server (ubuntu, pytest), server-windows (windows-2022, pytest). Uses cmake with LLAMA_BUILD_BORINGSSL=ON and GGML_SCHED_NO_REALLOC=ON. Tests via tools/server/tests/requirements.txt with pytest.

Docker image build CI. Creates and pushes git tags, generates build/merge matrices, builds multi-platform images (linux/amd64, linux/arm64, linux/s390x) for cpu, cuda (12.8, 13), rocm, vulkan, musa, intel, openvino backends. Builds full/light/server targets. Uses registry cache and QEMU for cross-platform builds.

Main CI workflow with 25+ build jobs: macOS (arm64/x64, Metal, WebGPU), ubuntu (cpu variants including s390x/ppc64le/riscv64, Vulkan, WebGPU, WASM, HIP/ROCm, MUSA, SYCL, OpenVINO), windows (cpu-x64, openblas, vulkan, llvm-arm64, opencl-adreno, CUDA, SYCL, HIP), ggml-ci (low/high perf CPU tests on x64/arm64 with SVE, KleidiAI, Graviton4).

CANN (Ascend NPU) backend CI. Runs on openEuler with Docker containers (ascendai/cann). Matrix: x86/aarch64, chip_type 910b/310p, use_acl_graph on/off. Builds with cmake -DGGML_CANN=on, SOC_TYPE, USE_ACL_GRAPH.

Vulkan backend CI. ubuntu-24.04 with llvmpipe. Sets up Vulkan SDK from LunarG, builds with cmake -DGGML_VULKAN=ON, runs tests with GGML_VK_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0, GGML_VK_DISABLE_F16=1, GGML_VK_DISABLE_COOPMAT=1. Uses ccache.

CPU-only Docker image. Ubuntu 24.04 base, gcc-14, cmake build with GGML_NATIVE=OFF, GGML_BACKEND_DL=ON, GGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS=ON. Three targets: full (includes CLI, tools, python, pip), light (llama-cli only), server (llama-server with health check).

CUDA Docker image. nvidia/cuda container (default 12.8.1), gcc-14, cmake build with GGML_CUDA=ON, GGML_BACKEND_DL=ON, GGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS=ON, supports CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES override. Same full/light/server targets as cpu.Dockerfile.

ROCm (AMD) Docker image. rocm/dev-ubuntu-24.04:7.2.1-complete, cmake build with GGML_HIP=ON, GGML_HIP_ROCWMMA_FATTN=ON, AMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx908/gfx90a/gfx942/gfx1030/gfx1100/etc. Same full/light/server targets.
Vulkan Docker image. Ubuntu 26.04, cmake with GGML_VULKAN=ON, glslc, libvulkan-dev. Uses uv (astral.sh) for Python package management in full target. Same full/light/server targets.

Nix packaging for llama-cpp. Supports CUDA, ROCm, MetalKit, BLAS, Vulkan, MPI, RPC backends via cmake flags. Configures CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES from cudaPackages, CMAKE_HIP_COMPILER for ROCm. Metal precompilation workaround with xcrun. Maintained by philiptaron and SomeoneSerge.

Nix flake interface. Imports .devops/nix/nixpkgs-instances.nix, apps.nix, devshells.nix, jetson-support.nix. Exposes packages: default (CPU), vulkan, windows (mingw), python-scripts, cuda, mpi-cpu, mpi-cuda, rocm. Runs formatter (nixfmt-rfc-style) and checks. Pins nixpkgs/nixos-unstable and flake-parts.

Project README. LLM inference in pure C/C++. Features: quantization (1.5-8bit), CUDA/HIP/Vulkan/SYCL/CANN/MUSA/WebGPU/Metal backends, CPU+GPU hybrid inference. Supports 70+ model architectures (LLaMA, Mistral, Mixtral, DBRX, Qwen, Phi, Gemma, etc.) and multimodal (LLaVA, Qwen2-VL, Pixtral, etc.). Tools: llama-cli, llama-server (OpenAI-compatible API), llama-perplexity, llama-bench. Extensive binding and UI ecosystem.

Contribution guidelines. 3-tier contributor model (contributors, collaborators, maintainers). AI usage policy prohibits fully AI-generated PRs. Guidelines: CPU-only for initial model PRs, test perplexity/performance, run test-backend-ops for ggml changes, separate PRs per feature, use squash-merge with <module>: <commit> format. Coding: snake_case, 4 spaces, <class>_<method> naming, enum UPPER_CASE with prefix.
One-line file pointing AI developers to AGENTS.md for guidelines before starting work.

Build documentation. CPU build (cmake), BLAS (OpenBLAS/oneMKL/BLIS), Metal (macOS default), SYCL (Intel GPU), CUDA (with CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES), MUSA (Moore Threads), HIP (AMD ROCm), Vulkan (Linux/Mac/Windows with LunarG SDK), CANN (Ascend NPU), ZenDNN (AMD EPYC), KleidiAI (Arm), OpenCL (Adreno), Android (NDK), WebGPU (Dawn), OpenVINO, IBM Z (zDNN). Context struct and sequence management. Defines the llama_context class with members for model reference, compute parameters, memory management, sampling, and backend scheduling.

KV cell management structures. Implements llama_kv_cells class managing individual KV cache cells with position tracking, sequence membership (bitset), and multi-sequence support.
Main context for LLM inference. Manages model, compute parameters, memory subsystem, sampling, backend scheduling, and graph computation.
Micro-batch structure holding token sequences, positions, embeddings, and sequence IDs for a single inference step.

Key-Value cache implementation. Manages ring buffer of KV cells, handles slot allocation/finding, builds graph operations for KV copy, and supports sliding window attention.
Manages individual KV cells with position, sequence membership (bitset), shift tracking, and 2D spatial positions for M-RoPE.
Incremental Sliding Window Attention cache. Chains base and SWA llama_kv_cache instances for layer-specific caching.
Batch allocator that sanitizes input batches, auto-generates positions/sequence IDs, and splits batches into ubatches.
Parameters for graph building including architecture, hyperparameters, compute params, ubatch, memory context, samplers, and graph reuse logic.

Graph building context. Provides build methods for normalization, FFN, attention, embeddings, recurrent states, and hybrid memory inputs.
Abstract base for graph inputs. Derived classes handle embeddings, positions, attention KV indices, attention KV ISWA, recurrent states, and sampling.

Vocabulary structures and functions for tokenization. Defines llama_vocab with token data, tokenizer model types (SPM, BPE, WPM), and pre-tokenization types for 50+ model families. Provides tokenization, detokenization, and BPE rank lookup.

Tokenizer implementations: SentencePiece (SPM) using bigram frequency merging, BPE using priority queue merge ranking, and WPM. Supports 50+ model-specific pre-tokenization regex patterns (Llama3, GPT2, DeepSeek, Qwen2, Gemma4, etc.). Includes naive trie for token lookup and byte encoding.

Sampler interface with chain pattern. Defines llama_sampler_chain structure holding multiple sampler instances. Supports backend initialization for GPU samplers and pre-allocated buffers for performance.

Sampling strategies: greedy (argmax), multinomial/distribution, temperature scaling, top-k, top-p (nucleus), min-p, tail-free, typical, softmax, frequency/presence penalties, repetition penalty, dry testing, classifier-free guidance, cache-based sampling. Ring buffer for history. Partial sort for top-k efficiency.

Grammar-constrained decoding structures. Defines grammar element types (CHAR, CHAR_RNG, RULE_REF, TOKEN, etc.), grammar stack for pushdown automaton, partial UTF-8 handling, and lazy grammar trigger patterns with regex.

Grammar parser implementing BNF-like syntax. Supports character ranges, repetitions (*, +, ?), alternations, rule references. UTF-8 decoding/encoding, grammar stack advancement for token acceptance, candidate rejection for constrained decoding.
Chat template enumeration with 55+ template types for models including Llama2/3/4, Mistral, ChatGLM, DeepSeek, Phi, Gemma, Granite, and more.
Chat template implementation and auto-detection. Maps Jinja-like templates to enum values. Applies role-based message formatting (system, user, assistant, tool) with model-specific special tokens.
Quantization declarations header. Empty in this version - implementation details in llama-quant.cpp.

Model weight quantization (Q4_0, Q4_1, Q5_0, Q5_1, Q8_0, IQ variants, K-quant types). Tensor categorization (attention Q/K/V/output, FFN up/gate/down). Importance matrix support, tensor type fallback for incompatible shapes, multi-threaded quantization.
LoRA adapter structures: llama_adapter_cvec (control vectors) and llama_adapter_lora with tensor weight pairs (A, B matrices), scale calculation, aLoRA support.

LoRA adapter loading and application. Parses GGUF metadata, validates architecture match, handles per-device tensor allocation, supports tensor shape validation for token embeddings vs. standard layers.
Unicode utilities: codepoint flags (letter, number, whitespace, punctuation, NFD), UTF-8 length/encoding/decoding, NFD normalization, Han character detection, regex-based splitting.

Unicode implementation with flag lookup tables, byte-to-UTF8 mapping for BPE encoding, custom regex split handlers for GPT2 and Llama3 pre-tokenization patterns, K2 trigger pattern handler, NFD normalization.
Unicode data declarations: codepoint range flags, whitespace set, case mapping tables, NFD decomposition ranges. 1.1M possible Unicode codepoints.

Generated Unicode data tables: 7000+ lines of static codepoint range flags, whitespace character set, lowercase/uppercase mapping tables, NFD decomposition ranges covering CJK, emoji, and special scripts.
Vocabulary class managing token-to-ID and ID-to-token mappings, token attributes, tokenizer model type (SPM/BPE/WPM), and pre-tokenization configuration for different LLM families.
Process of converting text to token IDs. Supports SentencePiece (byte-pair fusion), BPE (frequency-based merges), and WordPiece tokenization. Pre-tokenization regex varies by model family.
Byte-Pair Encoding tokenizer using priority queue for merge rank ordering. Pre-tokenizes text with Unicode regex, then iteratively merges highest-frequency adjacent pairs based on vocab lookup.
SentencePiece tokenizer using max-heap bigram frequency merging. Splits text to UTF-8 codepoints, then greedily merges highest-score adjacent pairs.
Composable sampling pipeline where multiple samplers are chained together. Each sampler transforms the probability distribution in sequence (e.g., temperature, top-p, penalties).
Selects token with highest logit/probability. Deterministic, fastest sampling method.
Random sampling from probability distribution using softmax-normalized logits. Supports both CPU and GPU (backend) execution.
Restricts sampling to k highest-probability tokens before random selection.
Nucleus sampling - selects from smallest subset of tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds threshold p.
Filters tokens below min_p * max_probability threshold, then samples from remaining.
Divides logits by temperature before softmax. Lower temp = sharper distribution, higher = more uniform.
Subtracts frequency-based penalty from token logits based on how often they appeared in generated text.
Binary penalty subtracted from logits of tokens that have been generated at least once.
Applies score discount to previously generated tokens to discourage repetition. Uses ring buffer for sliding window.
Constrains token selection to those valid under a BNF-like grammar. Uses pushdown automaton (grammar stack) to track valid continuations. Supports lazy grammars with trigger patterns.
Formats multi-turn chat messages with role tags, special tokens (BOS/EOS), and system prompts according to model-specific templates.
Reduces model weight precision (FP16->Q4/Q5/Q8) for memory/speed. Uses importance matrices for quality, supports IQ (integer) and K-quant types.
Low-Rank Adaptation - injects trainable rank-decomposition matrices (A, B) into frozen model layers. Scales by alpha/rank ratio.
Per-layer direction vectors that modify model behavior without full LoRA. Applied via element-wise addition to activations.
NFD (canonical decomposition) normalization for consistent Unicode representation before tokenization.
Variable-length encoding for Unicode: 1-4 bytes per codepoint. Used for byte-level BPE and grammar character matching.
Grammar testing mode that simulates token sequences without model inference. Used for grammar validation.
Sampling technique combining conditional and unconditional logits: logit = guided_logit + strength * (guided_logit - unguided_logit).

Interface for managing memory context during batch processing with next(), apply(), get_ubatch(), and get_status() methods.
Core memory interface implementing batch init, updates, sequence ops, state persistence, and memory breakdown.
Hybrid memory combining llama_kv_cache (for attention) and llama_memory_recurrent (for recurrent layers) via delegation.
Context for hybrid memory batch processing, wrapping both attention and recurrent context objects.
Hybrid memory variant using llama_kv_cache_iswa for sliding window attention combined with recurrent memory.
Context for iSWA hybrid memory processing, managing base/swa attention contexts and recurrent context.
Recurrent state memory for SSM models (Mamba/RWKV) managing R/S tensors and cell-based sequence tracking.
Context for recurrent memory providing tensor accessors and state copy information for graph building.
Per-cell metadata for recurrent cache: position, source indices, tail pointer, and sequence ID set.
Combines two memory statuses, returning failure if either fails, success if at least one updates.
Returns true if status indicates a prepare or compute failure.
Constructor initializing recurrent cache with R/S tensors per layer using ggml backend buffers.
Finds contiguous memory cells and places ubatch state, handling sequence sharing and state copying.
Validates that all ubatches fit in cache by simulating find_slot without modifying state.
Serializes recurrent state to IO interface, writing cell ranges and R/S tensor data.
Restores recurrent state from IO interface, reconstructing cell metadata and tensor data.
Resets all cache cells and optionally clears tensor data buffers.

nodes.description: Common base-class interface definitions and registration macros for all LLM model graph builders (llm_build_* classes), including llm_graph_context, llm_build_mamba_base, llm_build_delta_net_base, llm_build_rwkv6_base, llm_build_rwkv7_base, and ~70 model-specific build classes.
Implements the LLaMA 1/2/3 architecture via llm_build_llama<embed>, building a standard transformer with RMS norm attention, RoPE, optional KQ norm, and FFN (with optional MoE routing).
LLaMA with Incremental Sliding Window Attention (ISWA) via build_attn_inp_kv_iswa, supporting per-layer RoPE frequency scaling and sigmoid-gated shared experts in MoE layers.
Mistral 3 architecture implementation using standard RMS-norm attention and MoE FFN support, similar to LLaMA but with optional temperature scaling via attention scale.
DeepSeek v1 architecture with standard RoPE attention and a hybrid FFN: dense FFN for the first n_layer_dense_lead layers, followed by MoE with a shared expert and optional sigmoid gating.

DeepSeek v2/v3 architecture implementing Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) with QKV compression (wqkv, wkv_b), optional LoRA KV (wkv_a_mqa), YaRN RoPE scaling, and hybrid dense/MoE FFN with shared experts and expert weight normalization.
Qwen v1 architecture with a fused QKV projection (wqkv+bqkv), Neox RoPE mode, standard RMS FFN, and GQA support via head_kv.
Qwen v2 architecture with separate Q/K/V projections (with optional bias), separate RMS-norm FFN, and support for output bias on the lm_head.
Qwen v2 Vision-Language model adding ggml_rope_multi for Multi-Head RoPE (MRoPE) with 4 positional sections to support interleaved text and vision tokens.
Qwen v2 MoE architecture with standard RoPE attention and MoE FFN using softmax gating, featuring a gated shared expert (sigmoid-gated SiLU FFN branch).
Qwen v3 architecture with Q/K RMS norm (attn_q_norm, attn_k_norm), optional quantization scales (wq_s, wk_s, wo_s), and optional FFN quantization scales.
Qwen v3 Vision-Language model with MRoPE (ggml_rope_multi), Q/K RMS norm, and deepstack layers that add intermediate embeddings back into deeper layers for enhanced vision-language fusion.
Qwen v3 MoE architecture combining Q/K RMS norm, optional quantization, and MoE FFN with softmax gating and optional FFN quantization scales (no shared expert).

Qwen v3.5 architecture extending llm_build_delta_net_base with hybrid recurrent/attention layers via build_inp_mem_hybrid, implementing gated delta net (SSM) linear attention alongside standard attention, MRoPE, Q/K norm, and a gated output projection.
Qwen v3.5 MoE architecture combining the delta net hybrid attention mechanism from Qwen 3.5 with MoE FFN (softmax gating, shared experts, gate-up fused routing), and MRoPE support.

Qwen v3 Next architecture with hybrid attention using build_inp_mem_hybrid, implementing gated delta net (SSM) linear attention with convolution states and L2-normalized Q/K, gated output projection (sigmoid), and conditional MoE/dense FFN with shared expert gating.
Qwen v3 VL MoE architecture combining vision-language MRoPE (ggml_rope_multi), Q/K RMS norm, deepstack layers, and MoE FFN with softmax gating.

Main LLaMA graph builder (non-embedding mode). Builds standard transformer with: token embeddings, RMS attention norm, RoPE-ext Q/K projections (optional bias/quant), attention with KV cache, residual FFN (MoE or dense), final RMS norm, and lm_head projection.
LLaMA graph builder in embedding mode, using build_attn_inp_no_cache instead of KV-cached attention. Produces embeddings without lm_head logits output.
LLaMA ISWA graph builder with incremental sliding window attention, per-layer RoPE frequency scaling, optional temperature tuning, and MoE with sigmoid-gated shared experts.
Mistral 3 graph builder with optional temperature scale on Q, standard attention with RMS norm, and MoE FFN branch.
DeepSeek v1 graph builder with dense FFN for early layers and MoE with shared expert and sigmoid gating for later layers.
DeepSeek v2/v3 graph builder implementing MLA with QKV compression, rope-aligned Q/K split (nope+pe), optional LoRA KV, YaRN RoPE scaling, and hybrid dense/MoE FFN with expert weight normalization.
Qwen v1 graph builder using fused QKV projection with bias, Neox RoPE, and standard dense FFN.
Qwen v2 graph builder with separate Q/K/V projections, optional per-projection bias, and dense FFN.
Qwen v2 VL graph builder with MRoPE (ggml_rope_multi, 4 sections) for vision-language token handling, and dense FFN.
Qwen v2 MoE graph builder with softmax-gated MoE FFN and a sigmoid-gated shared expert FFN branch.
Qwen v3 graph builder with Q/K RMS normalization, optional quantization scales on Q/K/V and FFN projections, and dense FFN.
Qwen v3 VL graph builder with MRoPE, Q/K RMS norm, and deepstack layers that residual-add intermediate embeddings into deeper layers.
Qwen v3 MoE graph builder with Q/K RMS norm, optional quantization, softmax-gated MoE FFN with quantization support, and no shared expert.

Qwen v3.5 graph builder with hybrid recurrent/attention layers (build_inp_mem_hybrid), delta net linear attention (build_layer_attn_linear), MRoPE, gated Q projection, Q/K norm, gated output, and dense FFN.
Qwen v3.5 MoE graph builder combining delta net hybrid attention with softmax-gated MoE FFN (with shared experts and gate-up fused routing), MRoPE, and gated Q/K projections.

Qwen v3 Next graph builder with hybrid attention (recurrent/standard), delta net with L2-norm Q/K, gated output projection, conditional MoE or dense FFN with shared expert gating, and optimized/legacy SSM input paths.
Qwen v3 VL MoE graph builder with MRoPE, Q/K RMS norm, deepstack layers, and softmax-gated MoE FFN.

data.name: gemma
data.summary: Google Gemma (original) model using RMSNorm, GELU FFN, and RoPE with extended attention factors. Uses input scaling by sqrt(n_embd) and attention output scaling.

data.name: gemma3
data.summary: Google Gemma 3 model with Q/K RMSNorm, per-layer RoPE frequency scaling, attention post-norm, and optional ISWA (interleaved sliding window attention) support via template parameter.

data.name: gemma-embedding
data.summary: Google Gemma embedding model variant with Q/K RMSNorm, no KV cache (uses build_attn_inp_no_cache), per-layer RoPE, and ffn_post_norm. Designed for embedding generation tasks.

data.name: phi2
data.summary: Microsoft Phi-2 model using LLM_NORM (LayerNorm), bias in QKV projections, combined wqkv projection with bqkv bias, FFN applied to normalized attention output (not attention output), and Q scaling to avoid precision issues.

data.name: phi3
data.summary: Microsoft Phi-3 model using RMSNorm, optional ISWA support via template parameter, rope_factors for extended 128k context, combined wqkv or separate projections with biases, and MoE support via ffn_gate_inp.

data.name: phi
data.note: File src/models/phi.cpp does not exist. Only phi2.cpp and phi3.cpp exist in the codebase. Microsoft Phi-1 is not separately implemented.

data.name: command-r
data.summary: Cohere Command-R model using LLM_NORM, optional Q/K RMSNorm (attn_q_norm, attn_k_norm), separate QKV projections with optional biases, and SILU FFN in parallel arrangement.

data.name: starcoder
data.summary: BigCode StarCoder model using LayerNorm, combined wqkv projection with bqkv bias, learned positional embeddings (pos_embd) added to input (no RoPE), and GELU FFN applied sequentially after FFN normalization.

data.name: starcoder2
data.summary: BigCode StarCoder 2 model using LayerNorm, separate QKV projections with optional biases, RoPE positioning, and GELU FFN applied sequentially after FFN normalization.

data.name: dbrx
data.summary: Databricks DBRX MoE (Mixture of Experts) model using LayerNorm, combined wqkv projection with clamping (f_clamp_kqv), standard attention, and MoE FFN with router (ffn_gate_inp) using softmax gating, shared expert up/down projections.

data.name: jamba
data.summary: AI21 Jamba hybrid SSM/Attention model extending llm_build_mamba_base. Alternates between Mamba state-space layers (n_head_kv==0) and attention layers, supports both standard FFN and MoE FFN, and notably uses no RoPE positioning.

data.name: baichuan
data.summary: Baichuan model with variant handling: LLM_TYPE_7B uses RoPE, LLM_TYPE_13B and UNKNOWN skip RoPE. Uses RMSNorm, separate QKV projections (no bias), and SILU FFN. Input positions are only built for 7B variant.

data.name: bloom
data.summary: BLOOM model with token-level normalization (tok_norm applied to input embeddings before first layer), combined wqkv projection with bqkv bias, no positional encoding, and GELU FFN applied sequentially with FFN normalization.

data.name: falcon
data.summary: Falcon model with LayerNorm, combined wqkv projection, RoPE, optional second attention norm (attn_norm_2 for Falcon-40B), and GELU FFN applied to attn_norm (not attention output). FFN input bypasses attention output for residual path.

data.name: falcon-h1
data.summary: Falcon-H1 hybrid Mamba2/Attention model extending llm_build_mamba_base. Combines Mamba2 state-space layer (build_mamba2_layer) with standard attention (build_attn), aggregates both outputs, then applies FFN with bias. Uses per-layer f_attention_scale.

data.name: gpt2
data.summary: GPT-2 model using LayerNorm, combined wqkv projection with bqkv bias, learned positional embeddings (pos_embd) added to input (not RoPE), and GELU FFN applied sequentially with FFN normalization.

data.name: gptneox
data.summary: GPT-NeoX model using LayerNorm, combined wqkv projection with bqkv bias, RoPE positioning, and conditional FFN arrangement: parallel residual (use_par_res=true) applies attention and FFN in parallel from normalized inputs, or sequential (use_par_res=false) applies them sequentially.

Implements the MosaicML MPT (MosaicML Pretrained Transformer) architecture: a standard causal decoder with pre-normalization (RMSNorm), grouped query attention with optional Q/K layernorm, and a GELU feed-forward network combined via residual addition.

Implements xAI Grok architecture: a causal decoder with RMSNorm pre-normalization, separate Q/K/V projection matrices (with bias), standard RoPE, and a hybrid MoE+FFN architecture where the MoE branch (softmax-gated experts) and a parallel GELU FFN are averaged and added to the attention output.

data.summary: Implements Meta Chameleon multimodal architecture: a causal decoder with RMSNorm or SwinNorm pre-normalization, optional Q/K layernorm, RoPE on Q and K, grouped query attention, and a standard SwiGLU FFN combined with residual addition; includes image-logit suppression to force text-only output.

Standard RoPE on Q and K

data.summary: Implements the ChatGLM architecture: a causal decoder with RMSNorm pre-normalization, optional combined or separate QKV projections with bias, RoPE on Q and K, grouped query attention, SwiGLU feed-forward network, and residual addition with a build_cvec output hook.
key_architectural_features: Optional combined QKV (wqkv+bqkv) or separate Q/K/V projections

data.summary: Implements the Snowflake Arctic architecture: a causal decoder with RMSNorm pre-normalization, separate Q/K/V projections, RoPE on Q and K, a standard SwiGLU FFN (parallel residual), followed by a separate MoE branch that processes the original attention input, with both branches summed together.

data.summary: Implements the Dream decoder architecture (derived from Qwen2): a causal decoder with RMSNorm pre-normalization, separate Q/K/V projections with bias, RoPE on Q and K, grouped query attention, a SwiGLU FFN, residual addition, and a build_cvec output hook for embedding output.

Implements the DOTS-1 architecture: a causal decoder with RMSNorm pre-normalization, Q/K layernorm followed by RoPE, grouped query attention, and a two-phase FFN strategy where early layers use standard SwiGLU while later layers (>= n_layer_dense_lead) use a MoE branch combined with an optional shared-expert (shexp) FFN.

data.summary: Implements the BitNet (1-bit weights) architecture: a causal decoder with RMSNorm pre-normalization, separate Q/K/V projections with quantization-aware LoRA (build_lora_mm with scale tensors), a sub-norm (subnorm) after attention output, and a three-stage FFN with subnorm between stages (up->subnorm->gate->subnorm->down).

Three-stage FFN with subnorm: up -> subnorm -> gate -> subnorm -> down

data.summary: Implements the Refact code completion model: a causal decoder with RMSNorm pre-normalization, separate Q/K/V projections, grouped query attention (no RoPE), a SwiGLU FFN, residual addition, and build_cvec output hook for embedding output.

Implements the SmallThinker architecture: a causal decoder with per-layer variable RoPE scaling, conditional RoPE application (n_no_rope_layer_step), separate Q/K/V projections, grouped query attention, and a ReLU-gated MoE FFN where expert routing probabilities are computed from the input embeddings (not from FFN input).
