layers.name: Public API
layers.description: The stable C/C++ API surface exposed to applications. Defines the main entry points: model loading, context creation, inference (encode/decode), tokenization, sampling, and batch management. This is the only layer applications should link against directly.

layers.name: Core Library
layers.description: Internal llama.cpp implementation: model loading, context management, KV-cache, graph building, vocabulary, sampling, batching, memory abstraction, quantization, adapters, Unicode utilities, and architecture registration. All compute graphs are assembled here and delegated to GGML.

layers.name: Model Implementations
layers.description: GGML graph builders for 130+ specific model architectures (LLaMA, Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeek, Gemma, Phi, RWKV, Mamba, BERT variants, diffusion models, multimodal, etc.). Each file defines a llm_build_* class that constructs the GGML computation graph for one architecture family, inheriting from base classes where appropriate.

layers.name: ggml Tensor Library
layers.description: The core GGML tensor computation library. Defines ggml_tensor, ggml_context, ggml_cgraph, 96 tensor operations (ggml_mul_mat, ggml_add, ggml_softmax, ggml_rope, ggml_flash_attn_ext, etc.), the graph allocator, GGUF file format, and the backend interface. This is the foundation upon which all model computation is built.

layers.name: ggml CPU Backend
layers.description: GGML CPU backend implementing all tensor operations with SIMD vectorization across x86 (AVX/AVX2/AVX512), ARM NEON, PPC VSX, RISC-V RVV, IBM s390x VXE/NNPA, LoongArch LSX, and WebAssembly SIMD128. Includes architecture-specific quantized matmul kernels, weight repacking, BLAS integration, thread pools, and NUMA support.

layers.name: ggml GPU Backends
layers.description: GPU-accelerated backends for NVIDIA CUDA (including ROCm HIP and MUSA), Apple Metal, Vulkan compute, Intel SYCL, Huawei CANN/Ascend, Qualcomm Hexagon DSP, IBM zDNN, AMD ZenDNN, Intel OpenVINO, BLAS (cuBLAS/OpenBLAS), WebGPU, OpenCL, and virtual GPU. Each backend implements the ggml_backend_i interface for device-specific tensor operations and kernel execution.

layers.name: Common Utilities
layers.description: CLI tools and shared utilities for llama-cli, llama-server, and other executables. Includes argument parsing, console I/O, async logging, file downloading (HuggingFace, URLs, Docker), HuggingFace cache management, HTTP client, chat session handling, sampling wrappers, speculative decoding (n-gram, self-speculative), chat PEG parser, generic PEG parser, JSON Schema to GBNF grammar converter, Jinja2 template engine (lexer/parser/runtime), reasoning budget, Unicode utilities, debug tools, and preset management.

layers.name: Python Tools
layers.description: Python scripts and package for model conversion to GGUF format. Includes HuggingFace-to-GGUF conversion, LoRA adapter conversion, legacy GGML-to-GGUF migration, tokenizer hash updates, and the gguf-py package providing GGUF file reading/writing, vocabulary handling, tensor mapping, quantization, metadata, lazy loading, and CLI utilities.

layers.name: Build and Infrastructure
layers.description: CMake build configuration, CI/CD workflows, Docker images, Nix packaging, code style configurations, and documentation files that define how the project is built, tested, packaged, and deployed across all supported platforms and backends.

tour.title: Project Overview and High-Level Architecture
tour.description: llama.cpp is a pure C/C++ LLM inference engine with minimal dependencies. It is organized into three main layers: (1) ggml/ — the vendored tensor-computation library providing quantized matrix ops, compute graphs, and hardware backends (CPU, CUDA, Metal, Vulkan); (2) src/ — the llama.cpp core that builds LLM forward passes on top of ggml, handles model loading, tokenization, sampling, and KV caching; (3) common/ — CLI utilities, chat templating, and embedding helpers. The project ships two main binaries built from these libraries: llama-cli for interactive/repo-style text generation and llama-server for an OpenAI-compatible REST API. All inference is driven through a small, stable C API defined in include/llama.h.

tour.title: The Public C API — include/llama.h
tour.description: The public API in include/llama.h defines the six core opaque types and their lifecycle functions. llama_model holds all weights, hyperparameters, and device assignments loaded from a GGUF file. llama_context holds the inference state: KV cache, compute graph, and thread pools. llama_sampler encapsulates token selection (temperature, top-k, top-p, penalties, grammar). llama_vocab holds the tokenizer mappings. llama_batch carries a set of tokens (IDs, positions, sequence IDs) to process in one forward pass. The main API sequence is: llama_backend_init -> llama_model_load_from_file -> llama_init_from_model -> (loop) tokenize -> llama_decode -> sample -> tokenize -> ... -> llama_model_free + llama_backend_free.

tour.title: Model Loading — src/llama.cpp and src/llama-model.cpp
tour.description: src/llama.cpp implements the C API entry points (llama_model_load_from_file, llama_init_from_model, llama_backend_init) and the device-memory fitting logic (llama_params_fit). The heavy lifting of GGUF parsing, architecture detection, tensor loading, and weight placement is in src/llama-model.cpp. This file contains a model struct with all weight tensors, layer structs for each transformer layer type, and architecture-specific graph builders for all 130+ supported architectures. It reads the GGUF metadata (hparams, vocab, RoPE params) and maps each named tensor from the file into a ggml_tensor in memory — handling quantization formats like Q4_K_M, IQ4_XS, MXFP4, etc.

tour.title: Architecture Registration — src/llama-arch.cpp and src/llama-arch.h
tour.description: src/llama-arch.h defines the master enums for all supported architectures (llm_arch: LLAMA, MISTRAL, QWEN, GEMMA, DEEPSEEK, etc.), all GGUF KV metadata keys (llm_kv), and all tensor role types (llm_tensor: TOKEN_EMBD, ATTN_Q, ATTN_K, ATTN_V, ATTN_OUTPUT, FFN_GATE, FFN_UP, FFN_DOWN, etc.). src/llama-arch.cpp registers the complete set: architecture name maps, KV name builders (LLM_KV helper), tensor name builders (LLM_TN), and per-tensor info (layer type, GGML op). When a new model is added, these are the first files to modify.

tour.title: Tokenizer — src/llama-vocab.cpp
tour.description: src/llama-vocab.cpp implements three tokenizer algorithms: SentencePiece (SPM) using byte-pair frequency merging, BPE using a priority queue for merge ranking, and WPM. It handles 50+ model-specific pre-tokenization regex patterns (Llama3, GPT2, DeepSeek, Qwen2, Gemma4, etc.) and supports byte-level fallback for out-of-vocabulary tokens via a naive trie for fast token lookup. The llama_tokenize function in the public API calls into this module. Special tokens (BOS, EOS, UNK, PAD) and control tokens are resolved from the GGUF file metadata.

tour.title: KV Cache and Batch Management
tour.description: src/llama-kv-cache.cpp manages the key-value cache: cell storage, slot allocation, and cache eviction/rotation for sliding-window and full-context attention. It handles both standard and interleaved sliding-window attention (ISWA) patterns. src/llama-batch.cpp provides llama_batch_allocr which sanitizes and splits incoming batches into micro-batches (ubatches) for parallel processing. This batching infrastructure is what enables efficient batched inference and prompt processing.

tour.title: Computation Graph Building — src/llama-graph.cpp
tour.description: src/llama-graph.cpp is where the neural network is assembled as a GGML compute graph. It implements llm_graph_context and llm_graph_result classes that build the DAG of tensor operations for every forward pass. Each layer type (attention, feed-forward, MoE, RoPE, RMSNorm, etc.) is wired as a sequence of ggml_* calls. The graph is device-agnostic — once built, it is handed to ggml's scheduler which dispatches operations to the appropriate backend (CPU, CUDA, Metal, Vulkan, SYCL). The llm_graph_context struct is architecture-specific, holding layer weights and intermediate tensor references.

tour.title: The GGML Tensor Library — ggml/include/ggml.h
tour.description: ggml/include/ggml.h is the foundation of everything. It defines 96 tensor operations (ggml_mul_mat, ggml_add, ggml_softmax, ggml_rope, ggml_flash_attn_ext, ggml_gelu, ggml_silu, etc.), 42 data types including 20+ quantization formats (Q2_K through IQ4_XS, MXFP4, NVFP4), the ggml_tensor struct, and the ggml_cgraph (compute graph) API. The core pattern is: create tensors with ggml_* functions (which only build the graph, no computation), then call ggml_build_forward_expand to finalize the graph, then ggml_graph_compute to execute it. ggml also provides automatic differentiation (backward passes) and an optimization API (AdamW, SGD).

tour.title: Backend Abstraction — ggml/include/ggml-backend.h
tour.description: ggml/include/ggml-backend.h provides the hardware abstraction layer. It defines ggml_backend_t (CPU, CUDA, Metal, Vulkan, SYCL, OpenCL, etc.), buffer types, device enumeration, and a backend scheduler for multi-device tensor parallelism. The scheduler can partition a computation graph across multiple GPUs and coordinate them with events. Plugin backends can be loaded dynamically from shared libraries. Each backend implements all 96 GGML operations for its target hardware. When llama_decode is called, ggml schedules and dispatches graph nodes to the active backend.

tour.title: CUDA Backend — ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu
tour.description: The NVIDIA CUDA backend lives in ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu (the main entry) plus mmul.cu (matrix multiplication), fattn.cu (flash attention), mmq.cu (memory-mapped quantization), and other specialized kernels. It uses cuBLAS for GEMM operations and custom CUDA kernels for attention, softmax, normalization, RoPE, and quantization/dequantization. The backend is compiled with NVCC and loaded as a plugin when CUDA is available. ggml/include/ggml-cuda.h exposes the CUDA-specific API for device selection and memory management.

tour.title: Metal Backend — ggml/src/ggml-metal/ggml-metal.metal
tour.description: The Apple Metal backend uses ggml/src/ggml-metal/ggml-metal.metal which contains GPU shader functions for all GGML operations (matmul, attention, softmax, norm, RoPE, quantization). The Metal backend is the first-class citizen for Apple Silicon, leveraging ARM NEON, Accelerate, and Metal frameworks. It is managed by the Objective-C++ driver in ggml/src/ggml-metal/ggml-metal.m, compiled as part of the main ggml library. Metal enables efficient LLM inference on MacBooks with M-series chips without any external GPU dependencies.

tour.title: Vulkan Backend — ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/ggml-vulkan.cpp
tour.description: The Vulkan backend in ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/ggml-vulkan.cpp implements all GGML operations via SPIR-V compute shaders, making it the cross-vendor GPU path for AMD, Intel, Qualcomm, and other GPUs that support Vulkan. Like the CUDA backend, it provides custom kernels for the most performance-critical operations and uses the ggml backend registration API. Vulkan enables llama.cpp to run on a wide variety of hardware from gaming GPUs to integrated graphics.

tour.title: Token Sampling — src/llama-sampler.cpp
tour.description: src/llama-sampler.cpp implements a rich sampler chain with over 15 sampling strategies: greedy (argmax), multinomial, temperature scaling, top-k, top-p (nucleus), min-p, tail-free, typical, softmax, frequency/presence penalties, repetition penalty, dry testing, classifier-free guidance (CFG), cache-based sampling, and grammar-constrained sampling. The llama_sampler_sample function in the public API applies the configured chain. Samplers can be chained (e.g., top-k -> temperature -> repeat-penalty). A ring buffer tracks token history for repetition penalties.

tour.title: Chat Templating and Auto-Parsing — common/chat.cpp
tour.description: common/chat.cpp implements chat session handling using a Jinja2 template engine (in common/jinja/) and a PEG parser (in common/peg-parser.cpp). It applies model-specific chat templates to format multi-turn conversations, handles tool calls and function-calling schemas, and supports reasoning/thinking modes. The chat-auto-parser system (common/chat-diff-analyzer.cpp) auto-detects the structure of chat template outputs by comparing template renders with/without parameters, enabling structured parsing of unstructured model outputs. Grammar-constrained decoding via JSON Schema (common/json-schema-to-grammar.cpp) ensures valid JSON output.

tour.title: Model Conversion — convert_hf_to_gguf.py
tour.description: convert_hf_to_gguf.py (~13k lines) converts HuggingFace model formats to the GGUF format that llama.cpp reads. It defines a ModelBase class and model-specific subclasses (TextModel, MmprojModel) that specify how to map HuggingFace tensors to GGUF tensor names, how to write vocabulary and metadata, and how to handle architecture-specific quirks. Adding a new model requires: (1) registering the architecture in src/llama-arch.h/.cpp, (2) adding tensor mappings in convert_hf_to_gguf.py with a new ModelBase subclass, (3) implementing the graph builder in src/llama-model.cpp. The script handles tokenizer conversion, config writing, and quantization during export.
